This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
The appeal is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on the ground of liability as well as the quantum of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 22.12.2006 at about 12.30 p.m., the claimant was transporting the flag pillar (dwaja sthamba) in the mini lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-6768 from Mottedoddi Village to Shivarapattana Village, when he reached near Jute Factory on Kanakapura Road, the driver of the lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent matter with high speed, due to which, the lorry dashed to the road side tree.
Hence, the claimant sustained injuries.
Therefore, the claimant has preferred claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company submitted that the claimant has traveled in the goods lorry as a gratuitous passenger.
Therefore, the risk is not covered as per the insurance policy for gratuitous passenger.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further, it is submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal holding that the claimant has sustained 100% functional disability is not correct since the doctor has United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Sri Nagaraj S/O Venkatagiriyappa on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190244153/
2 stated 30% of functional disability towards whole body.

sentences.text: Therefore, prays for modification of the judgment and award of the Tribunal both on these aspects.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. In the present case, from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant was transporting flag pillar (dwaja sthamba) in the lorry and at that time, the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.
Hence, the claimant sustained injuries.
It is stated that the claimant is a Sculptor by profession.
Therefore, he was taking flag pillar on the said lorry and has sustained injuries.
When this being the fact revealed from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant was traveling along with the goods in the lorry but not as a gratuitous passenger.
Therefore, as per Section 147 of the MV Act, the risk of the person who had sustained injuries while traveling being authorized representatives of the goods and met with an accident is covered.

Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation as admittedly there was existence of insurance policy as on the date and time of the accident.
7.

sentences.text: 3  8. From the evidence on record of medical evidences including the evidence of doctor-PW.2, it is proved that the claimant had sustained fracture of C-3 and C-4 spinal chord, C-4 bones affecting the fracture to his spinal chord.
Due to these injuries, the claimant's four limbs have become functionless.
Therefore, it is the opinion of the doctor that the claimant had suffered permanent physical disability of 65% and 30% to the whole body.
Even though there is no evidence that the claimant was Sculptor by profession, but it can be believed on all its preponderance of probabilities from the evidence on record.

Work of Sculptor requires active involvement of both upper and lower limbs but as per the medical evidence on record including the evidence of doctor, the four limbs of the claimant have become functionless and it is observed by the Tribunal that the claimant is not able to walk without stick and with the help of person.
Therefore, the claimant had suffered 100% functional disability.
The assessment of physical disability and functional disability are two different things.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has places guidelines how to assess the functional disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, as per the principles of law laid down in the judgment as above stated and considering the nature of injuries and disability sustained by the claimant and nature of the profession for livelihood is taken into consideration, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the claimant has suffered 100% disability and that is affirmed by this Court.

9. The age of the claimant was proved to be 45 years old and the appropriate multiplier applicable is '14' as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma and Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in (2009)6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma and Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has committed an error in taking the multiplier as '13'.
The Tribunal has considered that the claimant has suffered functional disability of 100% as his livelihood is depending upon others' income and said finding is confirmed.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head that 'the claimant has suffered 30% of physical disability', to this, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued that it is a double compensation awarded but considering the notional income taken by the Tribunal at Rs.3,000/- p.m. is lesser side.
Further, the Tribunal has not added income towards 'loss of future prospects in life' but can be added since the claimant has suffered 100% functional disability.

Further, considering the medical bills produced for Rs.21,219/- but the Tribunal has granted lesser amount towards 'medical expenses including the miscellaneous expenses like transportation, conveyance, food, nourishment, etc'.

Therefore,
considering all these parameters taken by the Tribunal in quantification of the compensation, the parameters awarded by the Tribunal is found to be lesser side.
Therefore, if parameters are correctly held while making the quantification of compensation then the compensation amount would be more but the claimants have not preferred any appeal.

Therefore, by considering the overall facts,
circumstances and evidence on record as discussed, whatever quantum of compensation, is found to be just, proper and reasonable considering the nature of injuries and disability sustained by the claimant.
Therefore, on this quantum of compensation also, no grounds are made out for interfering with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is liable to be dismissed.
